title: Brooks Raley brings left-sided consistency as Phillies rebuild bullpen: MLB trade grades
content:
The Athletic has live coverage of the 2026 MLB Trade Deadline.

Mets get: RHP Luke Gabrysh, OF John Spikerman

Phillies get: LHP Brooks Raley

Mets: B-
Phillies: A

Relievers are notoriously volatile year to year — performance-wise, anyway — but Raley has been an exception. This is his fifth season in a row with an ERA under 3.00. From 2022 to now, he has a 2.42 ERA in 209 games, with more strikeouts than innings and a 1.048 WHIP. He had Tommy John surgery in the middle of that run (2024) but has come back strong.

Raley has held lefties to a .186 average this season, with righties hitting 30 points better. If the Phillies meet the Dodgers again in October, the good news is that Raley has held down Shohei Ohtani (1 for 7) and Freddie Freeman (1 for 6). The bad news is that Kyle Tucker is 3 for 3 with a homer off him.

Spikerman is a speedy, switch-hitting outfielder with no power who has slashed .232/.376/.323 since being drafted from the University of Oklahoma in the third round in 2024. Gabrysh, a right-handed starter, has a 4.17 ERA since being drafted from St. Joseph’s (Pa.) University in the 15th round in 2024.

It’s a rental setup reliever, so the prices are almost always reasonable. The Mets evidently see something in Spikerman and Gabrysh, and maybe they’ll get help in time. The Phillies know what they’re getting in Raley, and he could help a lot in the moment. — Tyler Kepner

Mets: C
Phillies: B+

The Phillies rank 24th in the league in bullpen ERA, even with all-world closer Jhoan Duran silencing hitters in the ninth inning. In a span of a few minutes Monday morning, wily wheeler-and-dealer Dave Dombrowski added Raley from the Mets and Caleb Kilian from the Giants. That ought to help. Raley was a sixth-round pick by the Cubs back in the Mesozoic Era, and then bounced to the Twins, Angels, the Lotte Giants of the Korean League, the Reds, Astros, Rays, Mets and now the Phillies. That’s a lot of mileage on the 38-year-old’s left arm, but it’s still effective, even if his hard stuff clocks in at about 90 mph these days, and he’s mostly leaning on an 81-mph sweeper and an 87-mph cutter.

Let’s not make this more complicated than it is: Raley is adept at limiting hard contact. Raley has a 1.96 ERA. The Phillies needed a reliever like Raley. The sad Mets, at this point in a lost season, did not. — Zack Meisel
